anzsic_codes.name: On Selling Electricity and Electricity Market Operation

merger_description:
1GT Europe (Lux) S.à r.l. (**1GT**) proposes to (i) subscribe for newly authorised and issued shares in Amber Energy Holdings Limited (a newly established UK company) (**Amber UK**), and (ii) purchase existing shares from certain current shareholders in Amber Holding Corporation Pty Ltd (**Amber Australia**) (the **Acquisition**). Once established, Amber UK will hold the entire issued share capital of Amber Australia (together with its subsidiaries, **Amber**) and 1GT will hold a minority interest in Amber UK.  

1GT is a global climate-focused private equity growth fund managed by Morgan Stanley Investment Management. Its core mission is to invest in private companies in North America and Europe that collectively aim to avoid or remove one gigaton of carbon dioxide-equivalent emissions by 2050. 1GT acts through its general partner, Morgan Stanley AIP GP LP, which acts by its general partner Morgan Stanley Alternative Investments LLC. Morgan Stanley Alternative Investments LLC is a subsidiary under Morgan Stanley Investment Management Inc, which sits within Morgan Stanley, a global financial services firm providing investment banking, securities, wealth management and investment management services that is listed on the New York Stock Exchange.  

Amber Australia, via its subsidiaries, operates a cloud-based demand-flexibility software platform and is a licensed electricity retailer in Australia. Amber Australia and its subsidiaries supply subscription-based energy retail services, automated battery and electric vehicle charging optimisation technology, and related devices to Australian households under the 'Amber' brand. It has around 92,000 customers in Australia. Its core product combines dynamic, wholesale-linked electricity price passthrough with software that provides real-time price information and can automatically charge and discharge a customer's home battery, solar system or electric vehicle in response to real-time price signals. Amber licenses its technology to utility partners internationally.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition given:
a. there is no horizontal overlap between 1GT (and its
connected entities) and Amber Australia in the retail supply
of electricity, as well as demand-flexibility software or
related goods and services in Australia
b. there is a low risk of foreclosure or other concerning vertical
effects resulting from exclusionary conduct post-acquisition.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
